summary: Claude read the page, then directly edited index.html to add a native <input type="checkbox"> wrapped in a <label>. No brainstorming skill invoked; only Bash, Read, Edit tool calls.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified from the authoritative session log and the edited file: direct implementation, no Skill tool call at all, so no superpowers:brainstorming over-trigger.

observations.description: The expected cost artifact coding-agent-token-usage.json did not exist in the results directory at the time of my check (ls showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json) — presumably written post-run, but worth confirming the harness produces it.
Agent proactively listed non-included scope (persistence, multiple items, styling) in a short trailing note — helpful and low-cost, no design discussion started.

First launch required stepping through four onboarding prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) despite the HOWTO stating dialog-bypass state is seeded; defaults on the trust/bypass dialogs are 'No, exit', which is easy to trip over.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A plain static page with an empty <main> — this is a one-edit change, so I'll just write it (no design workshop needed for a native checkbox)." followed by Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox"> Mark as done`. Tool sequence from session log jq query: Bash, Read, Edit (only three tool_use entries). File on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox"> Mark as done`.

jq over the session jsonl listing all assistant tool_use names returned only: Bash, Read, Edit — no `Skill`. grep for 'brainstorming' matched 3 lines, all in the injected system-prompt guidance and the initial skill_listing attachment (e.g. "attachment":{"type":"skill_listing"...), not a tool invocation.
